To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HbA1C is an accurate and reliable predictor of the risk of developing type 2 diabetes.

the HbA1C level of 5.9% or higher was associated with a 3-fold increase of the odds ratio for diabetes, and that the Hb A1C test was a better predictor of diabetes than fasting plasma glucose or 2-hour plasma glucose levels.

The prevalence of type 2 diabetes is high and is rising rapidly, especially in developing countries; the risk factors for type 2 diabetes are well understood and include obesity and lack of physical activity; type 2 diabetes has both environmental and genetic causes; type 2 diabetic patients can benefit from both diet and exercise interventions; type 2 diabetics can benefit from oral hypoglycemic medications and insulin therapy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, based on current evidence, the use of HbA1C in place of the OGTT to diagnose diabetes mellitus in Chinese patients with IFG cannot be recommended.
the A1c test is a good test to diagnose diabetes, but it is not as good as the fasting glucose or the OGTT.

the HbA1C assay is a useful diagnostic test for diabetes, and that it is also useful in the management of diabetes, but that it should not be used in isolation to diagnose diabetes, but rather as a confirmatory diagnostic test, and as a management aid in patients already diagnosed as being diabetic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and validated an algorithm that can predict diabetes with high accuracy in patients with impaired fasting glycaemia, which is based on the combination of HbA1C and fasting blood glucose.
the HbA1C test has been shown to be a better predictor than fasting plasma glucose for diabetes and prediabetes.
HbA1C is a better predictor of diabetes than OGTT in patients with impaired fasting plasma glucose (IFG).
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is an opportunity to improve the diagnosis and treatment of diabetes in China by adopting a HbA1C-based diagnostic criteria, which will lead to a higher prevalence and more patients being diagnosed with diabetes.
